slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Keep buying in 2027 on a de-risked supply, pre-qualify a gated lease, and build no cell in 2027
Judged on four tests, not unit price, only buying with a de-risked supply fails none
–	Our starting hypothesis, a leased cell, failed three of the five conditions it needed
The owned cell is not a 2027 option
–	It needs $7.3M against the $5.0M capital limit and leaves ~$3.2M of cash, below the $4.0M floor
–	The circulated $27 saving is $16 per good housing in 2027; payback is 3.7 years at 100k units (7.2 at 65k)
Leasing is a cost near-tie that turns negative if any one assumption slips
–	It saves $0.3M (1%) over 2027–29 in the plan, but costs $1.4M more on conservative demand
–	It costs $0.5M more if it runs 7 months of 2027 on full fixed cost; break-even is 207k units in 2028–29
Delivery reliability is a supply-design problem that buying can fix faster than any cell
–	The 0.2-percentage-point shortfall (96.8% on time against 97%) traces to one flood closure
–	Four supply levers act in 0–13 weeks, against 5–9+ months for a cell, for $0.25M capital and ≤ $0.72M working capital
Pre-agreed gates would switch to the lease; act before the March 2027 quote expiry
–	Triggers: committed 2028–29 volume of 208k+, a price above ~$84 (~$74 with committed volume) or on-time delivery under 97% for two quarters
–	The plan keeps 2027 year-end cash near $8.2M, enough to fund the lease if a gate trips
